missed_issues: Missing <torch/all.h> header in dsv3_router_gemm_entry.cu — the file added TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL_EXPAND which depends on <torch/library.h> macros, but the file only included core/registration.h which doesn't provide those definitions. Flagged by gemini-code-assist bot, addressed in follow-up commit before merge.

trivial_change_silence.notes: Correctly predicted silent human approval and fast merge. The skill's core prediction — that mechanical pattern-following changes from established contributors get approved without substantive human review — was exactly right. The only comment came from an automated bot, not a human reviewer.

key_insight: The trivial_change_silence skill works well for outcome and triage prediction. However, even mechanical changes can have subtle correctness issues (like missing headers) that a bot or careful reviewer might catch. The skill correctly focuses on predicting human reviewer behavior but doesn't account for automated review bots that may flag real compilation issues.
hypothesis: The missed header issue reveals a gap: when predicting 'zero comments' for trivial changes, we should still scan for completeness of the mechanical pattern being applied. The TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL_EXPAND macro requires <torch/library.h> or <torch/all.h>, and one of the modified files didn't have it. A skill focused on 'include/import completeness when moving code between files' could catch this class of issue. However, since this was only flagged by a bot and didn't block merge, the practical impact is low — the trivial_change_silence skill's core value proposition (predicting fast human approval) remains strong.
